easy.def: To hit with a flat hand.
examples: I smacked the fly.
She smacked the water.
He smacked his hands.

more.def: To hit something with the flat of your hand, making a sharp sound.
examples: She smacked the water with her hand.
He smacked a fly on the window.
The wave smacked against the rocks.

easy.def: Not big.
examples: A mouse is small.
I have a small dog.
This shirt is too small.

more.def: Little in size, or less than usual.
examples: A small stream ran through the forest.
She ordered a small cup of juice.
Only a small number of students stayed after school.

easy.def: Good at learning and thinking.
examples: She is smart.
A smart dog learns tricks.
That was a smart idea.

more.def: Quick to learn and good at thinking or solving problems.
examples: Crows are smart birds that can solve puzzles.
It was smart to bring an umbrella.
She is a smart student who loves math.

easy.def: To make neater.
examples: She smartened her desk.
He smartened up.
They smartened the room.

more.def: To make something look neater and smarter.
examples: She smartened up her desk.
He smartened his appearance for the party.
They smartened the room with fresh paint.

easy.def: In a neat and sharp way.
examples: She was smartly dressed.
He smartly saluted.
They marched smartly.

more.def: In a neat, quick or clever way.
examples: The boy was smartly dressed for the party.
The band marched smartly down the street.
She smartly answered the hard question.

easy.def: A clever person who likes to show it.
examples: He is a smarty.
The smarty knew the answer.
Don't be a smarty.

more.def: A person who likes to show how smart they are.
examples: He was a smarty who answered every question.
Don't be a smarty about it.
The smarty raised his hand first.

easy.def: To break something into many pieces.
examples: The glass will smash.
He smashed the plate.
The ball smashed the window.

more.def: To break something with a loud crash.
examples: The vase fell and smashed into pieces.
The wave smashed the sand castle.
He smashed the clay model by accident.

easy.def: A small amount.
examples: I know a smattering of French.
There was a smattering of snow.
A smattering of claps.

more.def: A small amount of something, spread out.
examples: I know a smattering of Spanish words.
There was a smattering of applause.
A smattering of raindrops fell.

easy.def: To spread something sticky or messy over a surface.
examples: I smeared butter on my bread.
He smeared the paint.
The baby smeared food on her face.

more.def: To spread something thick or sticky across a surface, often in a messy way.
examples: I smeared jam on my toast.
He smeared paint across the page by accident.
The baby smeared food all over her face.

easy.def: A messy mark left by something sticky.
examples: There is a smear on the window.
A smear of mud was on my shoe.
I saw a smear of jam.

more.def: A dirty or messy mark left on a surface.
examples: There is a smear of jam on the window.
A smear of mud ran down my shoe.
A smear of paint stained the shirt.

easy.def: To notice something with your nose.
examples: I smell cookies.
The dog smells the grass.
She smelled the flower.

more.def: To notice a scent with your nose.
examples: I can smell pancakes from my room.
The dog sniffed and smelled the whole yard.
She smelled the roses in the garden.

easy.def: To give off a scent.
examples: The soup smells good.
The trash smells bad.
Flowers smell sweet.

more.def: To give off a scent that people can notice.
examples: The bakery smells like fresh bread.
Wet dogs smell strong.
These roses smell sweet and lovely.

easy.def: What you notice with your nose.
examples: I like the smell of bread.
The smell is bad.
What is that smell?

more.def: A scent that you notice with your nose.
examples: The smell of pine filled the cabin.
A burning smell came from the toaster.
Dogs have a much better sense of smell than people.

easy.def: Having a bad smell.
examples: My socks are smelly.
The garbage is smelly.
A smelly cheese was in the fridge.

more.def: Having a bad smell.
examples: My gym socks were smelly after the game.
The garbage can was smelly on a hot day.
We held our noses near the smelly old cheese.

easy.def: To turn up your mouth to show you are happy.
examples: Smile for the picture.
She smiled at me.
The baby smiles.

more.def: To curve your mouth upward to show that you are happy or friendly.
examples: Everyone smiled when the puppy walked in.
She smiled and waved at her neighbor.
The baby smiled at her dad.

easy.def: A happy look on your face.
examples: She has a big smile.
His smile was bright.
There was a smile on her face.

more.def: A happy or friendly look in which the mouth curves upward.
examples: A big smile spread across his face.
She greeted us with a warm smile.
The baby's smile made everyone laugh.

easy.def: A little drawing of a smiling face.
examples: I drew a smiley.
A smiley on the card.
The smiley is yellow.

more.def: A simple drawing or symbol of a smiling face, often used in messages.
examples: She drew a smiley at the bottom of the note.
The teacher put a smiley on my paper.
He added a smiley to the end of the message.

easy.def: To smile in a sly, pleased way.
examples: He smirked at me.
She smirked when she won.
The boy smirked.

more.def: To smile in a pleased or sly way that is not kind.
examples: He smirked when he saw that I had lost.
She smirked at her secret.
The cat seemed to smirk after it ate the fish.

easy.def: Tiny little pieces.
examples: The vase smashed to smithereens.
The cup broke to smithereens.
The glass shattered into smithereens.

more.def: Very small pieces from something that has been smashed.
examples: The window shattered into smithereens.
The vase smashed to smithereens on the floor.
The sandcastle was blown to smithereens by the wave.

easy.def: A place where metal is shaped.
examples: The smithy is hot.
The blacksmith works in the smithy.
A smithy has a forge.

more.def: A workshop where a blacksmith shapes metal.
examples: The blacksmith hammered iron in the smithy.
Sparks flew in the smithy.
The village smithy was warm and noisy.

easy.def: A loose shirt that you wear to keep clothes clean.
examples: I wear a smock to paint.
The smock is big.
She put on a smock.

more.def: A loose, long shirt worn over clothes to keep them clean.
examples: I wear a smock when I paint.
The artist's smock was covered in color.
The baker wore a white smock.

easy.def: Dirty air that looks like fog.
examples: Smog covered the city.
The smog is gray.
Smog is bad for the air.

more.def: A kind of fog mixed with smoke or fumes that makes the air dirty.
examples: Smog covered the city and made it hard to see.
Cars make smog when there are too many of them.
A thick brown smog hung over the valley.

easy.def: The gray cloud from a fire.
examples: Smoke came from the chimney.
Fire makes smoke.
Smoke filled the room.

more.def: A gray or black cloud that rises from something that is burning.
examples: Smoke rose from the campfire.
Firefighters followed the smoke to the fire.
Smoke curled from the chimney.

easy.def: To give off a gray cloud.
examples: The chimney smokes.
The fire smoked.
The pot is smoking.

more.def: To send out a cloud of gray or black fumes.
examples: The chimney smoked on cold days.
The campfire smoked when we added wet wood.
The pan began to smoke.

easy.def: A building where meat is smoked.
examples: The smokehouse has meat.
A smokehouse is small.
The smokehouse smelled of smoke.

more.def: A small building where meat or fish is hung to be smoked and preserved.
examples: The ham hung in the smokehouse.
The old smokehouse smelled of wood smoke.
They smoked fish in the smokehouse.

easy.def: A tall pipe that lets out smoke.
examples: Smoke rose from the smokestack.
The smokestack is tall.
A smokestack on a ship.

more.def: A tall chimney on a factory, ship or train that lets out smoke.
examples: Smoke curled from the factory smokestack.
The ship's smokestack was painted red.
The tall smokestack could be seen for miles.

easy.def: Full of smoke, or tasting like smoke.
examples: The room is smoky.
A smoky smell.
The smoky air hurt.

more.def: Full of smoke, or having the taste or smell of smoke.
examples: The room was smoky from the burned toast.
The ham had a smoky flavor.
The campfire left a smoky smell on our clothes.

easy.def: To burn slowly with smoke but no flame.
examples: The fire smoldered.
The logs smolder.
Ashes smoldered.

more.def: To burn slowly with smoke but without a flame.
examples: The campfire smoldered all night.
Ashes smoldered in the fireplace.
The leaves smoldered in the damp air.

easy.def: Flat and even, with no bumps.
examples: The table is smooth.
The stone is smooth.
The road is smooth.

more.def: Having a flat, even surface with no bumps or rough spots.
examples: The pebble was smooth from years in the river.
The smooth ice made a good rink.
She sanded the wood until it was smooth.

easy.def: A thick drink made of blended fruit.
examples: I drank a smoothie.
The smoothie is cold.
Mom made a banana smoothie.

more.def: A thick, cold drink made by blending fruit, milk or yogurt and ice.
examples: Mom made a banana smoothie for breakfast.
The strawberry smoothie was cold and creamy.
I blended spinach and apple into a smoothie.

easy.def: To cover so much that there is no air.
examples: Sand smothered the little fire.
A blanket smothered the flame.
Don't smother the plant.

more.def: To cover something so completely that air cannot reach it, or to put out a fire by covering it.
examples: The firefighters smothered the small flames with a heavy blanket.
Weeds can smother young plants by blocking out the light.
She smothered her pancakes in syrup.

easy.def: A dirty mark where something was rubbed.
examples: There is a smudge on the glass.
A smudge of ink.
I wiped off the smudge.

more.def: A dirty or messy mark where something has been rubbed across a surface.
examples: There was a smudge of ink on my paper.
I wiped the smudge off the window with a cloth.
A smudge of chocolate was on his chin.

easy.def: To make a dirty mark by rubbing.
examples: Do not smudge the paint.
I smudged the ink.
She smudged the picture.

more.def: To make a mark messy by rubbing it.
examples: Be careful not to smudge the wet paint.
I smudged the ink when I rested my hand on the page.
She smudged the pencil lines with her thumb.

easy.def: Smeared and dirty.
examples: The window was smudgy.
A smudgy face.
The smudgy drawing.

more.def: Smeared with marks.
examples: The window was smudgy with fingerprints.
Her smudgy face needed a wash.
The smudgy writing was hard to read.

easy.def: Too pleased with yourself.
examples: He wore a smug grin.
She looked smug.
The smug cat sat on the chair.

more.def: Showing too much pride in yourself, as if you are better than others.
examples: He wore a smug grin after beating everyone at the game.
The cat looked smug as it sat in the sunny window.
Do not be smug when you win; be kind.

easy.def: To take something secretly where it is not allowed.
examples: The kids tried to smuggle a snack in.
She smuggled the cat in.
He smuggled cookies out.

more.def: To take something secretly into or out of a place where it is not allowed.
examples: The kids tried to smuggle a snack into the movie.
She smuggled the kitten into her room.
He smuggled a cookie out of the kitchen in his pocket.

easy.def: A person who sneaks things across a border against the rules.
examples: The smuggler hid the goods.
A smuggler in the story.
The smuggler sailed at night.

more.def: A person who secretly takes goods into or out of a country in a way that breaks the law.
examples: In the pirate tale, the smuggler sailed his boat into a hidden cove at night.
A smuggler hid the goods in a secret compartment.
The border guards caught the smuggler.

easy.def: In a way that shows you are pleased with yourself.
examples: He smiled smugly.
She smugly said, "I told you."
The cat sat smugly.

more.def: In a way that shows you are very pleased with yourself.
examples: He grinned smugly after winning the game.
She smugly said, "I told you so."
The cat sat smugly on the best chair.
